function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
**Reykjavík – the clear winner for an ice‑hockey‑focused trip** | Why Reykjavík stands out | What you’ll find there | |---------------------------|------------------------| | **Home of the national league** – The top‑tier Icelandic Hockey League (IHL) plays its home games at the *Íþróttahúsið* (Sports Hall) in Reykjavík. | • 2–3 games per week during the season (Oct–Mar).
• Modern indoor rink, good seating, and a lively atmosphere. | | **Largest fan base** – Reykjavík’s population (~130 k) means the crowds are bigger and the rivalry between local teams (e.g., *Íshúsfélagið* and *Hrafninn*) is intense. | • More merchandise, fan zones, and post‑game meet‑ups. | | **Convenient access** – Keflavík International Airport is only ~30 min away, and public transport (buses, taxis, rideshare) runs frequently to the arena. | • Easy to combine with other Reykjavík attractions (Harpa, Hallgrímskirkja, Laugavegur). | | **Cultural blend** – After a game you can enjoy Iceland’s vibrant nightlife, craft beer bars, and the famous “Blue Lagoon” day‑trip. | • Great food scene (seafood, Icelandic lamb, local brews). | | **Seasonal events** – The city hosts the annual *Icelandic Ice Hockey Festival* (usually in December), featuring exhibition matches, youth clinics, and a “Hockey Night” party. | • Perfect for fans who want more than just a single game. | ### Quick travel tips | Tip | Detail | |-----|--------| | **When to go** | Late October to early March for the full IHL season. | | **Tickets** | Buy online via the Icelandic Hockey Association website or at the arena box office. Prices are modest (~$10–$15). | | **Accommodation** | Stay in the city center or near the arena (e.g., Hotel Borg, CenterHotel Plaza). | | **Transport** | Use the “Ráðhús” bus line (no. 1) or a taxi; the arena is within walking distance of the city center. | | **Other sports** | If you’re interested in other winter sports, consider a side trip to *Þórsmörk* or *Skaftafell* for skiing or glacier walks. | --- #### Bottom line While smaller towns like Akureyri also host IHL games, Reykjavík offers the most comprehensive ice‑hockey experience—more games, larger crowds, better facilities, and the convenience of a major city. If you’re planning a trip centered on Icelandic ice hockey, Reykjavík is the place to be.
